theory.title: Verbos modales de obligación, consejo y permiso
theory.explanation: Usa must y have to para expresar obligación; mustn't para prohibir; don't have to cuando algo no es necesario; y should u ought to para aconsejar. Could y may hacen que las peticiones suenen más educadas.
theory.tip: Mustn't = prohibición; don't have to = no es necesario; should = consejo.

content.passage: Good friendships need care, honesty and respect. You should listen when a friend needs to talk, and you ought to keep promises. You don't have to share every interest, but you do have to respect each other's boundaries. You mustn't repeat something private without permission. If you make a mistake, you should apologise rather than make excuses. Friends may disagree, but they can usually find a fair compromise. Support works both ways: you can count on a good friend, and they should be able to count on you.

items.prompt: Describe how you usually get to know someone new.
items.modelAnswer: I usually get to know new people by joining in with a group activity. At a cooking class, for example, it is easy to ask others about a recipe and share ideas. Doing something together makes the first conversation less difficult.

items.prompt: Explain what makes a friendship strong.
items.modelAnswer: A lasting friendship is built through small actions, not just big promises. My closest friend remembers important dates, checks how I am and tells me honestly when I am making a mistake. We respect each other's time and differences.

items.prompt: Talk about a misunderstanding and how it was resolved.
items.modelAnswer: A friend once thought I had cancelled our plans because I didn't want to see him. In fact, my train had been cancelled and I couldn't contact him. When we finally spoke, I explained what had happened and we arranged another day.

items.prompt: Describe how you would solve a disagreement.
items.modelAnswer: I would avoid trying to win an argument. Instead, I would explain what matters to me and ask what matters to the other person. If we both make a small change, we may find an answer that works for everyone.

items.prompt: Explain how you prefer to receive important news.
items.modelAnswer: When I have good news, I like sharing it face to face because I can see the other person's reaction. If the news is difficult, I prefer a private conversation rather than a group chat. The situation should decide the way we communicate.

items.prompt: Give advice to someone who has fallen out with a friend.
items.modelAnswer: I would advise someone to contact their friend and admit that the relationship matters to them. They could say what upset them, but they should also ask how the other person felt. It is better to discuss one problem calmly than bring up every old argument.

items.prompt: Describe a time when you had to ask a difficult question.
items.modelAnswer: I once asked my manager whether I could change my working hours to attend an evening course. I explained why the course was important and suggested a different schedule. I was relieved when we found an arrangement that suited the team.

items.prompt: Explain how people can communicate respectfully online.
items.modelAnswer: To communicate well online, people should be clear about what they mean and avoid sending messages when they are angry. They should not share private photos or conversations without permission. If a topic is sensitive, a call may be better than a text.

items.prompt: Talk about a person you can rely on and why.
items.modelAnswer: My cousin Elena is someone I can depend on because she is practical and thoughtful. When I moved to a new flat, she helped me organise the boxes and stayed until everything was ready. She also listens without judging me.

items.prompt: Describe a conversation that changed your opinion.
items.modelAnswer: A discussion about public transport changed my opinion. I used to think that buses were always slower than cars, but a friend showed me how much time he saved by using a direct route. I now check public transport before driving.
